utterances.text: All right. Now, please tell us, did the republic or, rather, republican authorities, have any competencies in terms of command and control over the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The armed forces were unified and were under the command of the federal secretary for national defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did the republic or province authorities -- no. Let us take it this way: Was there a Vojvodina TO staff?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was there a Serbia TO staff?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was there a Kosovo TO staff?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who appointed their commanders?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The federal secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did the Republic of Serbia, or let's take Vojvodina, for example, did they have any authority to appoint TO Staff Commanders for Serbia or Vojvodina respectively?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did they have authority to exert command over those forces?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Command was single. They had no authority of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the specific case or, rather, the specific time to which this overview relates, did those -- were those TO units under JNA command or under any command of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were exclusively under the command of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Mr. Nice asked you if you knew that I had removed Kosovo from the agenda in Dayton. Do you know that Kosovo never featured on the Dayton agenda?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nice claimed that all those who were appointed at that time just before the war and during the war were Serbs. What is your ethnicity, General?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am an ethnic Hungarian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Questions were asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not what I asked. Of course I know this witness is ethnic Hungarian. It's well recorded in many documents, not least the SDC records where the accused speaks about him. What I asked was whether those who this witness appointed in the tabs that he produced were Serbs, and the answer to that was, clearly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Proceed. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, Mr. Nice produced to you an enactment that was sent by the department for defence of Pristina addressed to you personally. Sector for civilian defence, General Geza Farkas. Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They say here at the beginning: "We asked the command of the 3rd Army to provide us with weapons and ammunition for all units for -- that the authorities in Kosovo and Metohija are establishing and developing, namely detachments of Territorial Defence, communications units, civilian protection --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit 248.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is this a reference exclusively to legal authorities that exist in keeping with the law, civilian defence, civilian protection, communications units, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. And for all of them there existed appropriate establishment, materiel and personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, avoid leading questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether it's a leading question if I ask that the units of civilian defence, civilian protection and communications units were legal units envisaged by the law. I am asking the witness whether the law envisages such units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think this is the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say -- it says: "The said weaponry will be exclusively kept in depots of the army of Yugoslavia," and then I won't go on reading any more, but it enumerates which depots of the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was regulated that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that that weaponry requested for those legal units would not even be issued to them without an appropriate order that can follow only if necessary?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does it say in the last paragraph: "We emphasise that execution, distribution and issue to individual military conscripts --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot follow this without the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the interpreters are having difficulty following it without the document. Mr. Prendergast, can you locate the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The last paragraph. Last page. Next page. The first paragraph there. Yes, I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General Farkas, is it clear that these orders would be issued only in the event that mobilisation plans are put into effect, that are subject to verification by the defence department?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely the way it was regulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nice asked why in that case civilian population receives such weapons.

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we can see from this order that civilian population receives weapons only in case of mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in the event of mobilisation, does this civilian population cease to be civilian population?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. They are military conscripts, and once they are mobilised, they become members of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, since Mr. Nice asked you if you meant to say -- or, rather, if these people who are mobilised were prone to hatred and animosity, whether that would be dangerous to mobilise them, what is your opinion? Were they imbued with hatred towards Albanians?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They did not hate Albanians, and we did not have any cases where such people would react in that way within the system of command and control over them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, tell me, is there any enactment, regulation, or rule or principle according to which local population would not be subject to mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the contrary. There is a legal requirement by category of population, by age group, by professional training, et cetera, who should be mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it a rule that civilian protection and civilian defence units draw their personnel through mobilisation precisely from local population?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is a basic principle of civilian protection and defence. The people engaged there should know well the area where they work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So if I understand you, Colonel General, that rule was not a new one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It's not a rule. This is from the law where the material obligations and the work obligations of the population are regulated. So this is where the civilian population participates. In the first two, they are mobilised as a priority into the army, into the units of the MUP, and the units of the civilian protection. As for the rest, the military-aged able-bodied population, for example, to civil defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That law existed before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. On the basis of that Law on Defence, the formations were developed and this entire structure that we refer to here was all done on the basis of that law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Milosevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, Mr. Nice claimed that the police of the Republic of Serbia was militarised. As an educated, trained general, can you confirm that position of his that the police in Serbia was militarised?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I even asked him what he meant by that. I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nice showed you some document of the government of the Republic of Serbia and Montenegro, and he claimed that there is no institution called the Supreme Command Staff. Did somebody just invent the Supreme Command Staff or, in wartime, is the General Staff actually the body that grows into the Supreme Command Staff?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it. With the reduction in the personnel of the General Staff, in peacetime there are more people on the staff, and in wartime there's less people involved, so then there is the establishment of the General Staff in the war. And then when there is a state of war, it is no longer called the General Staff, it is called the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Supreme Command Staff. Is that something that somebody invented or is it based on regulations?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's based on regulation. And all documents during the course of the war have these exact headings and signatures and this has become part of documentation on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to go into the background of what was written in this document quoted by Mr. Nice, I just wanted us to establish whether this was an invented institution, the Supreme Command Staff. General, they also put questions to you about the Joint Command. You said this was a form of coordination. I'm not going to ask you anything else about that, but this form of coordination, did it in any way infringe upon the singleness of the chain of command in the army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In no way did it do so. Quite simply, it is not possible for it to infringe upon the chain of command. That is quite clear. It was quite simply impossible for something like that to happen, especially not in wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. General, Mr. Nice mentioned, in connection with General Vasiljevic's testimony, that representatives of the military at that meeting held in my office on the 17th of March gave information about some 800, and you said that the representatives of the military were talking about 200 something and the police about 300 something. Did anybody refer to this figure of 800?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that meeting only these two figures were mentioned; 200 something committed by our side, and 300 something was what the police said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In position -- or, rather, what was said what should be done with the persons who perpetrated these crimes?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was said unequivocally that they should be arrested momentarily and that they should be brought before a court of law without any delays. That was your position and your order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You said towards the end of your answer, when you were responding to questions pertaining to General Gojovic's material, that Ojdanic immediately ordered General Gojovic to establish to what level the procedure had come. You weren't clear enough. What procedure were you referring to in relation to these crimes that had been committed?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the procedure in terms of where the cases actually were. Quite simply, for Gojovic to make an overview as to how many crimes of this kind do we know of and where are these cases, and what stage of resolution are they in? Are they still in the state of investigations or pre-investigation or have they come to trial or have judgements already been passed? If not belonging to our own jurisdiction, have they been handed over to the judiciary?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Irrespective of the stage involved, in all these variants that you referred to just now, was this a procedure of criminally prosecuting the perpetrators of crimes in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. That is what the point of all of it was, to make an analysis of this kind and then to encourage the fastest possible resolution of those problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I don't know if the accused is finished, but there is just one point: The document he was referring to, which is the filing of Serbia and Montenegro, I haven't asked for it to be admitted because, of course, it's already before the Court, but he misrepresented what the document said. It didn't deny the existence of the Supreme Command Staff but it denied the existence of the Supreme Command and dealt with the way the word "Supreme Command Staff" may have been used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to say that I don't understand this. What is being denied? What is not being denied? I clearly put a question to the general whether somebody invented the word "Supreme Command Staff" or whether it was based on regulations and he gave an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, Mr. Nice put questions to you in relation to some alleged statement before a court of law of the former chief of state security, Radomir Markovic, that there was some meeting held in my office and that orders were given to remove bodies. Do you know that Radomir Markovic never gave such a statement before a court of law?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No. That's not an admissible form of question and indeed I think I prefaced my questioning about this with the circumstances before this Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic, the last question not permissible. Ask another question, or reformulate it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, if it's not permissible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, on the basis of everything that was published in this respect, that Radomir Markovic denied this assertion made by Mr. Nice when he testified under oath here and when he testified in Belgrade and before the committee of the parliament of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll have to remember now, but as for the previous things you mentioned before the Assembly and the Court, I think that's correct. I cannot remember exactly all the things that he stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know his statements that he had been tortured and that the other side had given him promises?

utterances.speaker: GEZA FARKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... just remind the Court, the issue of this statement is to be dealt with by this Court on the basis of evidence given by Markovic himself but also by those who took the statement, and who both have been before the Court, and I don't see how these questions can do anything to help the Court at the moment and probably they're irrelevant and inadmissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I agree, Mr. -- I fully agree, Mr. Milosevic. Move on to another question. In any event, we are past the time for adjournment, so bring your re-examination to a close as quickly as possible, bearing in mind the health of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have concluded. Thank you, I have concluded, Mr. Robinson. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milosevic. Let me just say that the document tendered by Mr. Nice at the end of cross-examination is admitted as Exhibit 921, tab 10. Colonel General, that concludes your testimony. Thank you for attending at The Hague to give it, and you may now leave. We are adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 11th day of November, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.05 p.m.
